races.name: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle on Saturday, August 29th Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Boston Common
runners_data.note: A 6yo hold-up horse for Seamus Neville and J J Slevin with a poor recent record (UP62/0) and a tendency to fade in the finish; genuinely wants to come late but the sheer volume of rear-rankers here means he is likely to race mid-pack rather than off the bridle at the back, which further dilutes his chance.

runners_data.name: Casper Charlie
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 5yo with a sparse form string (0-F) and two runs on Good going yielding no wins or places; a tendency to fade late combined with no meaningful evidence of improvement makes him hard to recommend in a competitive 19-runner field.

runners_data.name: Coral Reid
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 5yo with unknown going profile and no recent outing recorded; Tom Kelly (7) rides and the E McNamara yard sends out Tumbling In in the same race, so stable confidence likely lies elsewhere — treat with caution until more is known.

runners_data.name: Goodmancon
runners_data.note: PJ Breen's 6yo has shown glimpses of ability with two placed efforts from 13 runs on Good ground, but his natural instinct is to race off the pace; mapped here to midfield due to the overcrowded hold-up group, he is effectively racing out of his preferred role and the STYLE_FIT discount applies.

runners_data.name: Installment
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes the ride for W J Lanigan on this 6yo who has been out 11 days and is a genuine hold-up performer, but with five straight runs on Good yielding no wins, his proximity to the pace is unlikely to be voluntary — he is pushed to midfield by circumstance rather than by choice, and that compromises his chance.

runners_data.name: Minella Moon Shine
runners_data.note: John J Nallen's 6yo ran a solid second on his hurdles debut on Good and steps back up with Daniel King aboard; a prominent-racing profile suits this shape well, and a single start returning a placed effort on matching going makes him one of the more interesting unearthed types.

runners_data.name: Rodeo Joe
runners_data.note: Paddy Cody (7) takes on a 6yo who has been off 389 days and carries a string of pulled-up efforts; the extended absence is a significant concern, and only a chaotic race that plays to patience would make him relevant.

runners_data.name: Ruled By The Sun
runners_data.note: Ray Hackett's hold-up 5yo has run twice in 11 days and placed zero times from three starts on Good or similar; the quick turnaround is worth noting but form figures of 7-7P on the relevant ground offer little encouragement for a competitive maiden.

runners_data.name: Seven Towers
runners_data.note: Keith Donoghue partners Gavin Cromwell's 5yo who has placed four times from six runs on similar ground — a consistent and honest prominent racer who travels well and handles Good going; the combination of a reliable prominent style and a strong handler makes him one of the most interesting shapes in the race across multiple scenarios.

runners_data.name: Who's Going
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's 4yo has been off 122 days and carries weight from a modest recent form string (080-) on Soft and Heavy; a fades-in-finish flag and no runs on Good ground in the relevant profile make him difficult to enthuse over despite the powerful stable connection.

runners_data.name: Cool Native
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy partners Gordon Elliott's lightly weighted 6yo (159lbs) who has placed three times from four runs on Good; a prominent-racing style and solid record on matching going makes him one of the most plausible pace-tracking threats, and the Kennedy-Elliott axis in a maiden of this nature commands respect.

runners_data.name: Louve d'Arc
runners_data.note: William Harvey's 5yo was off 140 days and has no wins from three starts on Good or Heavy; a hold-up racer who has never threatened in the finish, she would need an unusually messy race to feature.

runners_data.name: Maple Mornin
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in the field, Eoin Staples (5) rides for DM Christie in a horse who finished ninth on debut on Good going; a fades-in-finish flag means she is vulnerable to being swallowed late, but with no rival expected to contest the lead, she controls tempo entirely and that is a significant tactical advantage.

runners_data.name: Star Cave
runners_data.note: Patrick Foley's 6yo has tongue-tie and a placed effort over 24f on Good going; the unknown style flag means her positioning is uncertain, but a single piece of encouraging form at the right distance and going is worth noting for each-way purposes.

runners_data.name: Tumbling In
runners_data.note: E McNamara's 5yo has placed in three of four runs on Good ground and stays the distance well; a hold-up racer who is consistent without winning, she represents the most reliable closer profile in the field and is best served if a genuine pace develops.

runners_data.name: Xquise
runners_data.note: Cian Collins' 6yo has been off 594 days following a flat career that produced no wins; the enormous absence, fades-in-finish flag, and no jumps form on record make this a very speculative runner.

runners_data.name: Carrigane
runners_data.note: Donncha Duggan's 6yo has placed once from five runs on Good and was last seen 50 days ago; a natural hold-up horse placed into midfield by the crowded rear group — the redistribution is a structural concern rather than a reflection of intent, and the modest record limits his appeal regardless.

runners_data.name: Kalico Leader
runners_data.note: Edward Buckley's 7yo has lightly raced status with unknown going profile and no jockey named; a placed effort and fall in three starts provides thin evidence, and the long absence (92 days) adds risk.

runners_data.name: Siege Of Milan
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's 6yo has no recorded form and no jockey assigned; entirely unknown quantity on debut and must be treated as a wild card with no basis for assessment.

races.paceDynamic: Maple Mornin is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-horse maiden hurdle over 2m4f at Roscommon on Good ground, and with no rival likely to contest the lead aggressively, she is set to dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the front without being pressured. Behind her, Seven Towers, Minella Moon Shine, and Cool Native should slot into prominent positions just off the pace, giving the race a clear lead-and-chase structure rather than a chaotic scramble. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the map can physically accommodate at the rear — Installment, Goodmancon, Carrigane, and Boston Common are genuine closers by nature but are more likely to race mid-to-rear-of-midfield given the number of horses seeking that ground; only the most patient and well-placed among them will secure a true stalking berth. A sustainable, uncontested pace on Good ground over an extended trip strongly favours horses that travel prominently with cover or can make smooth headway from the middle of the field — true late closers launching from the back will need a stronger gallop than Maple Mornin alone is likely to generate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Maple Mornin sets a fair but unforced gallop and prominent horses like Seven Towers and Cool Native travel smoothly just behind.
scenarios.body: Maple Mornin dictates without fuss and the prominent racers conserve energy throughout, leaving them with enough in reserve to pounce turning for home on Good ground that rewards those who travel well throughout; horses racing in the first four or five are ideally positioned as the pace is unlikely to be truly searching.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely sedate and a horse sitting just off Maple Mornin produces a decisive mid-race move that the hold-up horses cannot bridge.
scenarios.body: A very slow early tempo turns the race into a sprint from the home turn, handing a decisive edge to any prominent horse quick enough to kick two out before the closers can organise their challenge; Seven Towers, with consistent placed form on Good and a competent pilot in Keith Donoghue, is ideally suited to capitalise on this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger than expected and enough gaps appear in the straight to allow a well-positioned mid-field horse to make sustained late headway.
scenarios.body: Tumbling In, who has placed in four of four runs on Good ground at this trip range, represents the profile best suited to this shape among the genuine closers, as she has the consistency and trip form to sustain a run from off the pace; Goodmancon and Installment carry redistribution discounts and are less likely to deliver this shape cleanly, making Tumbling In the primary beneficiary if it materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Attrition Late
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes crowding, interference at hurdles, or a faller disrupts the race shape materially in the back straight.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners over obstacles on a track that can become congested, any significant incident reshuffles the deck entirely and benefits horses wide or clear of trouble who have been produced patiently; Rodeo Joe and Louve d'Arc, racing fresh and without strong positional commitments, are among those who could profit from a messy race.

watchPoints.text: Maple Mornin controls the pace entirely as the only confirmed front-runner — watch whether Eoin Staples elects to inject pace at the top of the hill or conserves, as that choice will dictate whether closers can get back into contention.

Seven Towers and Cool Native are both aiming for the same prominent position just off the leader — if they jostle for that berth early, one of them will be forced wider or to use more energy than ideal, which could compromise both.

With 19 runners over hurdles at Roscommon, the early stages over the first few flights carry genuine interference risk — any horse caught wide in a pocket or brought down could reshuffle the entire race shape without warning.

Tumbling In's placed run at 23f on Good going is the most relevant piece of staying form in the hold-up group — watch how quickly gaps appear in the straight if the pace is genuinely honest, as her chance depends entirely on it.

Installment and Goodmancon are both natural hold-up horses riding with Danny Mullins and Ian Power respectively who are unlikely to be in their preferred position — observe whether either can be produced with a clear run in the straight or whether traffic becomes a decisive factor.

races.name: James Lohan Engineering Excellence Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Clay Pigeons
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins runner returning after 198 days off but has won over similar Good ground; travels prominently and a clean-jumping display from Brian Hayes could see this gelding dictate from just off the early chaos.|

runners_data.name: Minella Hollow
runners_data.note: Won twice on Good ground at 16f and handles this trip well; Daniel King rides for a small yard posting a rare runner but the horse has strong form credentials and will press forward from the outset after 289 days off.|

runners_data.name: Earthwatch
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan handler freshened after 11 days; style is hold-up and has finished fourth repeatedly on Good ground, suggesting consistency without the finishing burst needed to win unless the pace is very strong indeed.|

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: Headgear noted; races out of handicap in maiden company and has flat form rather than jumps pedigree, making it hard to assess jumping ability — the apprentice rider and a long run of placed efforts on Good turf add little confidence at a big price.|

runners_data.name: Haughty
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer who has struggled to get competitive at this trip and further; form figures of PP in recent runs are a concern and the amateur rider is not the strongest asset in a competitive 19-runner maiden.|

runners_data.name: Captain Hanley
runners_data.note: Eamonn O'Connell's consistent horse has placed multiple times on Good ground over 20-24f, but its true natural style is hold-up and in this field of 19 with the rear congested by hold-up types, it is unlikely to secure an ideal position — STYLE_FIT tag tempers its chance.|

runners_data.name: Chantilly Wings
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has run creditably from the front; Carl Millar has ridden it recently and it finished second last time out, but competing against two other confirmed leaders in a maiden hurdle is a stiff ask.|

runners_data.name: Kilmond Knight
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse flagged for fading in the finish; recent form of P-U0 with limited Good-ground exposed form at Roscommon — the stamina question marks are significant given the pace this race will be run at.|

runners_data.name: Le Roi Arthur
runners_data.note: Kieren Buckley in the saddle; confirmed front-runner returning after 318 days off which is a significant layoff concern; placed at 18f on Good ground previously so the trip is fine if fitness is there.|

runners_data.name: Saviour Blu
runners_data.note: Prominent racer flagged for fading finishes; form of 0-U0 and three runs on Good ground all resulting in double-figure finishes make this a very difficult selection to support regardless of race shape.|

runners_data.name: Whoyougonnacall
runners_data.note: John Patrick Ryan yard with a notable recent runner count; prominent racer who has placed at 18f on Good ground and finished fourth and third in recent starts — consistent enough to be involved if pace scenario plays out favourably.|

runners_data.name: Direct Approach
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy in the saddle for Gordon Elliott is a strong jockey-trainer combination in a modest maiden; midfield hold-up style, 11 days since last run, has placed on Good ground over 19f — stamina appears solid enough for this shape.|

runners_data.name: Glenmore Graduate
runners_data.note: J J Slevin is a high-class jockey but this horse is lightly raced and flagged for fading finishes; Good-ground exposed form only twice and both runs resulted in well-beaten positions, making it hard to build a case.|

runners_data.name: Leva Deva
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish; only two exposed runs on Good ground, both resulting in poor finishes at 18f — Jack Gilligan rides but the evidence of stamina limitations is a concern over this demanding trip.|

runners_data.name: Prophetess Miriam
runners_data.note: Placed twice at 16f on Good ground and ran well again at 22f; prominent style suits the expected pace scenario and Eoin Walsh riding for Cian Collins who is in form with the yard — one of the more interesting long-shots on exposed form.|

runners_data.name: Speisialta
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner but recent form of 4-R0 with a refusal is a red flag; Anthony Black yard with a single runner in the last 14 days — the early pace role is likely but its reliability over hurdles is seriously questioned.|

runners_data.name: Ataboymiley
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell sends this unknown commodity out with no known last run date; style and going preference are unknown flags meaning there is no basis to project a race role — treat as an outsider with no meaningful form angle.|

runners_data.name: John Gun
runners_data.note: Kieran Purcell yard, unknown going preference and lightly raced flag; no last run date available and style is unknown — completely opaque from a form and pace perspective in this 19-runner field.|

runners_data.name: Goeasyonme
runners_data.note: John Patrick Ryan runner with unknown going preference and lightly raced; same trainer as Whoyougonnacall but no form to analyse — impossible to place within the pace map with any confidence.|

races.paceDynamic: Speisialta, Le Roi Arthur, and Chantilly Wings are all confirmed front-runners in a 19-runner maiden hurdle over 1m7½f on Good ground at Roscommon, virtually guaranteeing a strong early gallop with multiple horses competing for the lead from the outset. These three will push each other along through the early stages, setting a genuine pace that is likely to stretch the field and test stamina in the closing stages of this trip. Clay Pigeons and Minella Hollow are the most natural prominent racers and will look to settle just off the lead battle, while Direct Approach and Whoyougonnacall offer tactical versatility from midfield. The hot pace strongly favours horses who can travel comfortably in the first half of the race without being too close to the firing line — prominent-to-midfield types with proven stamina are best placed, while hold-up horses face an uncertain test if the pace collapses late; Captain Hanley is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed into a midfield slot because the rear of the field is overcrowded with natural hold-up types, meaning it is unlikely to secure its preferred position and its chance is tempered accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other off and a prominent racer picks up the pieces from just off the lead in the straight.
scenarios.body: The contested early gallop sets up a searching test of stamina and horses who settled just behind the leaders without expending energy in the pace battle will be best positioned turning for home; the 1m7½f trip on Good ground rewards those who travel fluidly and pick up when the front-runners cry enough.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfield Sweeps
scenarios.trigger: If the front three go too fast too soon and capitulate, leaving midfield horses to swoop through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: A breakneck early gallop at Roscommon can implode quickly if all three leaders try to dominate, creating a vacuum through which midfield horses travelling powerfully can storm late; this scenario particularly suits runners who have shown the ability to finish strongly on Good ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Clears
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pace-setters — most likely Le Roi Arthur or Chantilly Wings — asserts early and the others don't match their level of commitment throughout.
scenarios.body: Rather than a war of attrition between all three leaders, one settles into a rhythm that suits them and builds an unassailable lead before rivals can organise; this rewards any front-runner with superior jumping and enough residual stamina to hold on down the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly extreme and enough of the field fades to open a clear passage for a deep hold-up horse to finish off the race.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires genuine carnage at the front and clean runs through traffic — conditions that are possible but not probable given the field size of 19 and the tendency for Good-ground maiden hurdles to produce a moderately resilient pace; Captain Hanley's redistribution out of its natural role further reduces confidence in this shape delivering.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Speisialta jumps cleanly from the outset — a refusal in recent form means it is a genuine safety and race-shape risk if it causes interference at an early hurdle in a 19-runner field.

Monitor which of the three front-runners (Speisialta, Le Roi Arthur, Chantilly Wings) actually commits to the pace — if all three press hard from flag fall, the race could be run at a suicidal gallop, dramatically shortening the finish and opening the race up for midfield horses.

Clay Pigeons is returning from 198 days off for Mullins — if it moves powerfully into contention from the prominent position, it is a sign the horse is race-fit and should be tracked closely through the final two hurdles.

Direct Approach with Jack Kennedy represents a strong jockey booking for a midfield runner — watch whether Kennedy positions it closer than its style suggests; if he does, it may signal confidence from the Elliott yard.

With 19 runners and three confirmed leaders, the field is likely to spread wide early at Roscommon — watch the drawn positions and early traffic to see whether any midfield runners are blocked or lose ground at the first flight.

races.name: DNG Ivan Connaughton Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Born Bright
runners_data.note: Won twice over similar Good-ground trips and holds solid form at this level; a hold-up type who will need the pace to develop sufficiently over three miles to close from rear positions, and the controlled tempo is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Born Bright won two of her last five starts and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, giving her a solid claims here; the main concern is that she returns after 57 days off carrying 166 lb.

runners_data.name: Mephisto
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up performer returning just six days after a run, with a visor in the headgear record and modest recent form including a pulled-up; the short turnaround and lack of recent prominence are significant negatives.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up two outings back, Mephisto returns quickly on six days' rest; he has run over today's trip and going before, yet 165 lb is a stiff ask for a gelding yet to find his best form.

runners_data.name: Kalanisi Flash
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and race-shaper, fitted with tongue-tie and blinkers to aid concentration; a marked style-fit flag (0.93) applies as this horse has recently raced in a more restrained role, but in a race with no other confirmed pacemaker it effectively has a free lead.
runners_data.comment: Three consecutive pulls-up make Kalanisi Flash a serious concern, and a struggling yard (0/31 over 14 days) compounds the worry — yet he has experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 114 ranks him third of 18, underlining he retains ability on his best form.

runners_data.name: Sound Judgement
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott, who is in strong recent form (2/43 over 14 days); a genuine prominent racer whose Good-ground record and recent win make him well-suited to tracking the pace and challenging from the front two flights out.
runners_data.comment: Sound Judgement won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but she shoulders a hefty 161 lb and her trainer is in poor recent form — those are real drags on her chances of repeating.

runners_data.name: Starzov
runners_data.note: Returning from 352 days off the track with a tendency to fade in the finish; without racecourse fitness and given the stamina test over three miles, the layoff and documented finishing weakness are major concerns regardless of pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Starzov is winless in his last five starts and returns after a 352-day absence, yet he has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating of 118 marks him as the standout of 18 — the main concern is whether that lengthy layoff blunts his challenge.

runners_data.name: Mavetherave
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes a prominent ride for the O'Connell yard, though recent form figures are modest; this horse is likely to be competitive early and can secure a position near the pace, though the step up in trip to three miles needs to prove out.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Mavetherave does bring distance and going experience to the table, and 31 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; however, a top weight of 159 lb looks a stiff ask for a gelding whose recent efforts have been largely disappointing.

runners_data.name: Priory Park
runners_data.note: A hold-up veteran of ten who has been off for 108 days and whose recent form figures are largely poor; will need everything to fall right and a stronger pace than expected to get involved from off the bridle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up two outings back, Priory Park faces questions on consistency, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 108 suggests some residual ability — 108 days off the track is the bigger concern.

runners_data.name: Getaway Charlie
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer whose natural position is from the rear, but with so many true closers in this field it is unlikely to find that ground — the style-fit flag (0.92) and redistribution note both temper expectations significantly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts but there are reasons for optimism: he has run over today's trip and going before, and 29 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, with our rating of 117 giving him solid claims in this field despite carrying 158 lb.

runners_data.name: It's Not His Fault
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who fades in the finish and is a true hold-up type relocated forward on the map due to overcrowding at the rear; the fade flag combined with its out-of-role position makes it hard to fancy in any of the likely race shapes.

runners_data.name: Itsaworkinmaniam
runners_data.note: Returning from 296 days off, this hold-up horse by nature is mapped to midfield due to the surplus of closers; the long layoff is the dominant concern, and even if it finds a better position its finishing kick after such a break is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with promise when second two starts back, but that fall three starts back clouds his jumping profile, and 296 days off the track is a significant fitness question; has experience of today's going, though the sixth last time out suggests he's not firing at present.

runners_data.name: Mr Dibbs
runners_data.note: Won over 26f on Good recently for Cromwell and has place form at this trip; a hold-up type whose best form on similar ground makes it one of the more credible closer profiles if any pace develops — blinkers assist focus.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, but pulled up two starts back and again five starts back, so his completion record remains a concern; 84 days off the track and a trainer without a winner in 37 recent attempts are further negatives, despite his experience on today's going.

runners_data.name: Western Model
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 24f on Good ground with strong place consistency; a hold-up type who has won on this going and at this sort of trip, making it well-placed to capitalise if the race develops into a staying test.

runners_data.name: She'll Be Kept
runners_data.note: Won last time out 14 days ago for the McMahon yard (1/6 in 14 days); a true hold-up type placed into midfield on the map due to the rear-of-field surplus, so the style-fit penalty (0.93) applies — form is live but positional concerns are real.
runners_data.comment: She'll Be Kept won last time out and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround having run over today's going before, but her erratic recent record — a fall and an unplaced run among her last five — and a lowly ranking of 15th of 18 on our figures make her hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Glitz And Glamour
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer for McNamara with a 5lb claimer up; has placed on Good ground over 24f and can run forward, though recent form figures have been below par and the headgear absence is noted.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, including a pull-up, Glitz And Glamour is hard to fancy ranked 13 of 18 on our figures, though she has run over today's distance and going before and her 25-day break at least suggests she returns fresh.

runners_data.name: Sallap
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago, which is an obvious fitness query; a genuine hold-up type who fades in the finish, redistributed to midfield — the quick turnaround, stamina fade, and out-of-role position combine to make this a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Sallap won two of her last five starts, but returning just two days after her most recent fifth makes freshness a concern, and carrying 156 lb is a stiff burden; ranked 17th of 18 on our figures, she faces a steep ask here despite having run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Knocknagoran Lady
runners_data.note: Won twice in recent starts on Good ground and has strong course-going affinity; a natural hold-up performer placed forward on the map due to field congestion at the rear — the style-fit flag (0.93) tempers the live form angle.
runners_data.comment: Knocknagoran Lady has winning form in recent starts — back-to-back victories — but she sits at the foot of our rankings here, and 155 lb is a stiff burden to overcome against this level of opposition.

runners_data.name: Wild Mandate
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 26f and has placed repeatedly on Good ground; no jockey listed, which is a query, but the horse's profile suggests it can track the pace if the rider chooses to commit forward.
runners_data.comment: Wild Mandate returns just two days after being pulled up, and ranked 16 of 18 on our figures she faces a stiff ask; a winner two starts back shows she retains some ability, and she has experience of today's going, but the quick turnaround is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Smackwater Jack
runners_data.note: Twelve-year-old with consistent recent form including wins and places over 22-24f on Good; a prominent racer who can be expected to take up a close tracking position behind Kalanisi Flash and is well-suited to the controlled pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 18 on our figures, Smackwater Jack faces a stiff ask carrying 152 lb, and his sole win in his last five starts tempers enthusiasm — though he has run over today's trip and going before, and back-to-back placed efforts latterly show he retains some form.

runners_data.name: Its Not Over Yet
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with decent Good-ground form at this trip for McKiernan; redistributed to midfield due to the surplus of closers, and the style-fit flag (0.92) means its natural finishing move is unlikely to be executed from its actual race position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, though a third two runs back offers some encouragement; she has run over today's trip and going and arrives fresh enough at 29 days between runs, but 152 lb is a stern burden for a mare ranked 10th of 18.

races.paceDynamic: Kalanisi Flash is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field over 3 miles on Good ground, and with no confirmed rival willing to press from the front, this horse is set to control proceedings at a sustainable, unhurried gallop from flag to finish. Sound Judgement, Mavetherave, Glitz And Glamour, Wild Mandate, and Smackwater Jack will cluster prominently behind the leader, creating a compact early order rather than a true pace duel. The field carries a significant surplus of hold-up types — Itsaworkinmaniam, It's Not His Fault, Getaway Charlie, She'll Be Kept, Sallap, Knocknagoran Lady, and Its Not Over Yet are all genuine rear-of-field operators who are unlikely to secure their natural positions in a 19-runner field of this configuration, with Sound Judgement and Smackwater Jack best placed to lock in prominent berths behind the pacesetter. With one horse setting a controlled, uncontested pace over three miles on quick ground, the race shape heavily favours prominent racers who can travel sweetly in the slipstream, make their move jumping the final flights from a position of advantage, and hold on; true hold-up types who need a strong pace to set up a finish will be left wanting.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kalanisi Flash Controls; Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Kalanisi Flash dictates at a measured tempo and prominent horses track comfortably into the straight.
scenarios.body: Kalanisi Flash sets a manageable pace that rewards horses racing in the first four or five, and those prominent types who travel fluently will have first run from the last hurdle with enough petrol left to hold on up the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Lifts; Closers Get Home
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes incident or pace increases materially in the middle stages, stretching the field and opening the race up.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop would string out the field and allow the better-class hold-up performers to pick off tiring rivals in the final half-mile; Good ground at Roscommon favours the stayer who gets a true test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Pacesetter Escapes Field
scenarios.trigger: If Kalanisi Flash is allowed to build a substantial lead early and the prominent pack misjudges the tempo.
scenarios.body: The chasing group collectively underestimates the advantage ceded and Kalanisi Flash, finding minimal pressure, dictates fully and proves very hard to reel in at the finish; prominent types closest to the pace inherit the best placing opportunities.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Outrun Their Role
scenarios.trigger: If the field unexpectedly fractures early and redistributed hold-up horses manage to find their natural position further back than the map suggests.
scenarios.body: Several horses tagged as redistributed — Itsaworkinmaniam, She'll Be Kept, Sallap — would need a genuinely strong pace to deliver from the rear, and without it even those who find better positions than mapped will struggle to land the spoils.

watchPoints.text: Kalanisi Flash is the only confirmed pace-setter in a 19-runner field — if it jumps slowly or is taken off a clean lead by Sound Judgement or Smackwater Jack, the entire race shape collapses and the pace dynamic becomes unpredictable.

Sound Judgement and Smackwater Jack are both likely to press for prominent positions behind the leader; if both commit hard early, they could transform this from a controlled single-led race into a genuine pace contest that opens the door for closers.

Starzov returns from 352 days off the track — a horse of this profile can interfere with others if it makes jumping errors or drops quickly through the field in the final mile of a 3m race over hurdles.

Several hold-up types — including Sallap (ran 2 days ago), Knocknagoran Lady, and She'll Be Kept — have live recent form but face structural positional disadvantages; monitor whether any of these find a better position than the map suggests in the opening half-mile.

With 19 runners over 3m on Good ground, interference at the early hurdles is a genuine risk — horses like Mephisto (quick turnaround) and It's Not His Fault (fade flag) are ones to watch in the early stages for jumping errors that could impact those immediately behind.

races.name: J.F. Hanley Groundscare Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Hashtag Pretender
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with consistent Good-ground form (1W7P on similar going) and a recent fall to forgive; Flanagan partners a horse who has finished placed at this trip and is well-placed to track Impero before challenging — the most natural beneficiary of the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Hashtag Pretender shaped with real promise when third and second in two of his last three completed starts, and he has run over today's trip and going — the main concern is that fall last time out, now 59 days ago, which leaves a fitness and confidence question mark heading into this.

runners_data.name: Impero
runners_data.note: The race's only front-runner, set to dictate under Jack Kennedy from a powerful yard; Good ground and a beginners' context suits his role as pace-setter, and his recent form (placed in similar conditions) supports holding his position all the way to the line.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in recent starts with a second and two thirds in his last five, Impero has run over today's trip and going and rates the one to beat on our figures, though he remains yet to score.

runners_data.name: Killeemore Lad
runners_data.note: Showed a win and two places at 16-17f on Good recently and arrives fresh off just 13 days; a natural hold-up type who will be forced to race closer to the pace than suits him in this field of closers, which tempers how much faith to place in his finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive seconds two and three starts back underline Killeemore Lad's consistency, and he has run over today's trip and going, while 13 days between runs means he comes here on a quick turnaround; the fall last time out is the one flag to watch.

runners_data.name: Orkneys Jack
runners_data.note: Comes here off a pleasing 3rd in a 20f bumper/chase context and is unbeaten on his five runs on Good going; though a genuine hold-up horse by inclination, the lack of rivals ahead of him in the rear means he will likely find himself racing midfield rather than from his favoured rearmost pitch — his Amateur jockey (7lb claim) is also worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Orkneys Jack showed his best when winning three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going underlines his credentials as a genuine threat; the main concern is whether he can recapture that form after finishing fifth last time out.

runners_data.name: Piccolo Player
runners_data.note: A 5-year-old lightly-raced on Good ground with three placed efforts at 16-17f; genuinely wants to race off the pace but in this field of multiple hold-up types will not enjoy the uncontested back-of-the-field berth he needs, and his OR of 104 leaves him with most to find against the main rivals on ratings.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Piccolo Player faces a stiff task under 166 lb; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a third last time out at least shows he can get into the mix.

runners_data.name: Silent Selector
runners_data.note: Has winning experience on Good going over 20f and is the most credentialled of the hold-up horses in this race; Donoghue is an accomplished jump jockey who can organise a late run, but the lack of genuine gallop from Impero makes a clean passage from the rear inherently more difficult.
runners_data.comment: Silent Selector won five starts back but has posted four fifth-or-worse finishes since, suggesting inconsistency is the concern; he has run over today's distance and going before, and returns after 32 days off carrying 166 lb.

runners_data.name: Swing Time
runners_data.note: Returns from a 273-day absence which is a significant concern in a beginners' chase context; has never won on Good ground in five attempts on similar going, and even when fresh his form figures on the going (0W0P) offer limited encouragement — requires substantial improvement to be competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, the most recent of which ended in a pull-up 273 days ago, Swing Time arrives rusty, carrying 166 lb, and ranks last on our figures — experience on today's going offers little consolation given the overall profile.

races.paceDynamic: Impero, ridden by Jack Kennedy, is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner beginners' chase over 2m½f at Roscommon and figures to lead from the outset on Good ground with no rival likely to seriously dispute the pace. With no genuine challenger to push Impero into a headlong gallop, Kennedy can dictate a measured, energy-conserving tempo that will suit a horse whose form shows placed efforts at this sort of pace. The field behind Impero is heavily populated by hold-up types — Silent Selector, Swing Time, Killeemore Lad, Orkneys Jack, and Piccolo Player — meaning the race is likely to develop into a one-horse lead with a chasing pack bunched in behind, creating a scenario that heavily favours prominent and front-running profiles. This race shape is tailor-made for Impero to control and for Hashtag Pretender to track, with closers likely to find themselves too far back to deliver a meaningful late challenge from a muddling pace. Note: Orkneys Jack, Killeemore Lad, and Piccolo Player are genuine hold-up horses shown in midfield on the map because the field holds more come-from-behind types than the visualisation can place at the rear — Impero and Hashtag Pretender are overwhelmingly most likely to actually occupy the front positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Impero Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Impero is allowed to stride clear at a controlled pace and meets each fence accurately under Kennedy.
scenarios.body: Impero bowls along at a sustainable gallop that never hands the initiative to rivals, and the moderate tempo leaves chasers with insufficient runway to close the gap in the straight; Hashtag Pretender, the only genuine tracker, is the primary threat.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Impero makes a costly jumping error mid-race and Hashtag Pretender smoothly assumes the lead.
scenarios.body: Hashtag Pretender has the fitness and form (placed on Good ground multiple times) to cruise into contention and punish a front-runner who has handed away momentum; the controlled early pace means Flanagan's mount arrives full of running at the second-last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and the field dawdles to such a degree that closers get a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Silent Selector has the best winning form from off the pace and is the pick of the genuine hold-up types if a late rush materialises, but the single-pace scenario and bunched field makes a clean passage far from certain for Donoghue.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart — Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fencing errors cause a fractured race with several departures and a fragmented run-in.
scenarios.body: With several first-season chasers in a beginners' event, mishaps could scramble the order entirely and hand an opportunity to a horse who jumps cleanly and stays out of trouble; Killeemore Lad, despite being out of natural role, has the raw jumping ability to capitalise on a messy race.

watchPoints.text: Swing Time returns after 273 days off — watch for any signs of ring-rustiness or jumping anxiety at the first few fences, as a bad early blunder could compromise the entire field behind him.

Orkneys Jack's amateur rider (7lb claim) is untested in a competitive chasing context at this level — monitor whether he can hold a constructive position given his horse's natural tendency to want to be held up.

Impero's jumping accuracy is the pivot of this race — a single bad fence on the far side could hand Hashtag Pretender an unearned lead and restructure the entire outcome from Scenario A to Scenario B.

Killeemore Lad ran only 13 days ago; if Andrew Slattery's yard (4 wins from 37 in the trainer's 14-day window) has targeted this quickly, watch for signs the horse is sharper than his recent F (fall) suggests.

Good ground is confirmed throughout the card — no significant going drift is expected, so horses with proven Good-ground form (Hashtag Pretender 1W7P, Silent Selector 2W2P) carry reliable going profiles into this race.

races.name: Kepak Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Full Noise
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent racer handled by amateur Mr D McGill (7lb claim) for the McGill yard, who are 0/4 in the 14-day window; 758 days off is an alarming absence but good-ground sim record (9 runs, 2 wins, 2 places) is encouraging and the P style is ideal for the expected race shape — this is the profile the race favours most.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts, Full Noise nevertheless showed clear ability when second two starts back, and has run over today's trip and going — a combination that keeps him very much in the mix at a rating of 98. The significant concern is 758 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Gaoithe Glory
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up horse returning after 19 days for the McNamara yard, 0/5 in the 14-day window; good-ground form is thin (0 wins, 0 places from 8 similar-going runs), and sitting deep in a congested rear of 19 runners makes finding a clear run the primary obstacle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Gaoithe Glory nonetheless shows consistency with a pair of fourths and fifths in recent outings, has experience of today's going, and returns on a quick turnaround of 19 days; a mark of 92 and 165 lb to carry may test his chances of breaking that duck.

runners_data.name: Jouster
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a useful staying profile (4/5 last runs over 22-23f), back after 18 days for Paul Flynn with a 5lb claimer; good-ground figures (12/15 runs, 1 win, 2 places) suggest the surface is no issue, but the blinkers and tongue-tie suggest a controlling handler who knows this horse needs specific conditions to deliver.

runners_data.name: Island McCoo
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Donncha Duggan, Sean Flanagan in the plate — last win over 24f on Good, 11 days since last run suggesting fitness is peak; two wins and two places from 10 good-ground starts make him one of the more reliable closer profiles, though the bunched rear of this field is a clear navigation risk.
runners_data.comment: Island McCoo landed a win three starts back and was second four starts back, but has disappointed in both subsequent runs since, including a fourth last time out after just 11 days' rest; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, though a career-high 162 lb tests his resolve.

runners_data.name: Ladies Well
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (win 23 days ago over 23f Good) for the Slattery yard which is in excellent form (4/37 in 14 days); Darragh O'Keeffe riding is a major positive, and the hold-up style over a strong staying trip on good ground fits perfectly — needs traffic to clear in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Ladies Well won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but she carries a hefty 162 lb and our rating of 85 leaves her ranked 12th in a 19-runner field — talent is there, weight may blunt it.

runners_data.name: King's Son
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for JJ Slevin and Seamus Neville, six-year-old blinker-wearing sort who has posted three places from nine good-ground starts but no wins; the 13-day return is fine but a form string of 0-366 suggests he finds the right horse hard to beat rather than being the winner himself.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, King's Son steps back out quickly after 13 days, carrying 159 lb off a mark of 86; a third three starts back offers some encouragement, though two successive sixths since suggest he faces a stiff ask from 11th in the rankings.

runners_data.name: Another Challenge
runners_data.note: Returning after 75 days for the McKiernan yard, this is a genuine hold-up horse whose true racing position is deeper than the midfield slot he has been mapped to — with so many closers in the field, he is unlikely to achieve his natural running style, which limits his chance in any scenario where gap-finding is crucial.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts, Another Challenge steps up from a second two runs back but has looked inconsistent either side of it; 75 days off the track is a fitness query, though he has distance and going experience to call on.

runners_data.name: Dunany Point
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner and the architect of the pace shape; Kieren Buckley takes a 7lb claim mount for Conor David Maxwell, good-ground record is decent (12/15, 1 win, 5 places) and he carries the pace dynamic on his shoulders — his own chance depends on whether the gallop is sustainable enough to preserve his jumping rhythm into the closing stages.
runners_data.comment: Returned just 13 days ago and has run over today's trip and going, yet winless in his last five starts — including a pull-up — gives reason for caution; a third last time out offers a sliver of encouragement, though carrying 158 lb makes life harder for a runner ranked eighth of 19.

runners_data.name: Doyen Wolf
runners_data.note: Veteran 10-year-old flagged as a horse who fades in the finish; his real preference is to race from the rear, but with the hold-up berths oversubscribed he has been slotted into midfield — the finish fade flag and a modest good-ground record (0 wins, 1 place from 3 runs) mean this out-of-role positioning is a double handicap.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and pulled up two outings back, Doyen Wolf also arrives here 84 days off the track and ranked 14 of 19 on our figures; he has run over today's going before, but it's hard to make a strong case at 155 lb.

runners_data.name: Firstupbestdressed
runners_data.note: Another McGill runner (Mr O McGill, 5lb claim) with a finish-fade flag; genuinely wants to come from the back but is mapped to midfield due to the surfeit of closers — good-ground sim record is weak (0 wins, 0 places from 7 runs) and the UU (unseated) entries in recent form add jumping risk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and twice unseated in recent form, Firstupbestdressed does bring distance and going experience to the table, and his 21-day break looks fair; carrying 153 lb, however, is a significant burden for a horse ranked ninth of nineteen.

runners_data.name: Backinabit
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for Denis Hogan (2/32 in 14 days, active yard), blinkers fitted; won 17 days ago over 17f Good suggesting recent fitness but the step to 21f-plus on a right-handed track is a significant extension — mapped to midfield despite hold-up preference, so unlikely to secure a true position from which to finish.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up twice in recent starts and only eighth on his latest outing, Backinabit is hard to fancy ranked 16 of 19 on our figures; he does return quickly on familiar going, but his recent form makes him a tough sell at 151 lb.

runners_data.name: Ballyredinkingston
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for John Patrick Ryan (1/19 in 14 days), five-year-old claimer on board; four runs over 22-24f on Good showing 0 wins but consistent mid-field finishes — the prominent style fits the race shape, though form figures of 6,6 on most recent pair suggest a horse that gets close without threatening.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts — with two sixths, a bring-down and two unplaced efforts — Ballyredinkingston makes little appeal ranked 18 of 19 on our figures, though he has run over today's going before and returns after a 33-day break.

runners_data.name: Tantrum Boy
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a fade-in-finish flag, genuinely a hold-up horse but displaced to midfield; McMahon yard is 1/6 in the 14-day window but the form string (70-084) shows minimal impact, and the restricted good-ground record (0 wins from 4 runs) offers little encouragement for a racing-out-of-role scenario.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Tantrum Boy has experience of today's trip and conditions, but carrying 151 lb while ranked last on our figures makes him extremely hard to fancy despite a respectable 14-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Rideau Canal
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old for Denise Foster, 57 days since last run; a genuine hold-up type whose best win came on Heavy at Hereford over 22f — good-ground figures are undistinguished (0 wins, 0 places from 9 runs) and at this age, in a competitive field, asking him to navigate traffic from the rear is a tall order.
runners_data.comment: Rideau Canal has pulled up twice in his last three starts and has gone unplaced in between, making him desperately hard to fancy off 150 lb; he has run over today's distance and going before, and that sole win four starts back offers a distant crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Johnny M
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old flagged for finishing fade, naturally a hold-up horse pushed out of his ideal berth by the volume of closers in the field; McNamara yard is 0/5 in 14 days and recent form (70/00P) is nearly without encouragement, making a contribution unlikely regardless of race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up most recently, Johnny M faces an uphill task, though his experience on today's going and a strong 96 rating suggest latent ability — the risk is that recent form offers little to cling to.

runners_data.name: Max Time
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer with a fade flag for Madden yard (1/3 in 14 days); good-ground record is the weakest in the prominent group (0 wins, 0 places from 11 runs) and recent form includes two Ps — the tongue-tie fits a horse that needs restraint but the stamina profile over 2m5½f is questionable.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with two pulled-up efforts among them, Max Time is hard to fancy ranked 15 of 19 on our figures; some experience over today's trip and going at least counts for something, and 19 days ago suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Run For The Border
runners_data.note: Top-rated horse in the field at OR 95 for the John Patrick Ryan yard (1/19, 14 days); no jockey listed which is a flag to watch — hold-up style, won over 19f Good, placed over 22f Good and the recent 2-3 form on good ground is strong. Best hold-up profile in the race if the traffic clears.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and third two starts back, Run For The Border arrives on a quick 14-day turnaround with distance and going experience in her favour, though a hefty 168 lb burden and our rating of 91 suggest she faces a stiff ask against stronger-rated rivals here.

runners_data.name: Charlie's Gift
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for John Burke (0/1 in 14 days), 50 days off; form string ends in FP (fell, pulled up) and all five good-ground runs produced finishes of 7,7,8 — the combination of jumping risk and modest form makes this one to swerve in a busy field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up on his most recent outing 50 days ago, Charlie's Gift faces a stiff ask off 162 lb, though he has run over today's going before and our rating of 94 suggests there may be more to find.

runners_data.name: Not So Serious
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who won over 22f Good most recently for the Lanigan yard (1/5 in 14 days), showing he handles the surface and trip; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position at the rear is squeezed out by the density of closers, so his chance is partly a function of how well the field spreads and whether he can find racing room earlier than usual.
runners_data.comment: Not So Serious won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him the one to beat off a mark of 85 despite three pull-ups in his recent record — that latest victory is the form that matters here.

races.paceDynamic: Dunany Point is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and is expected to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop on Good ground over 2m5½f at Roscommon — a setup that gives him full control of tempo from the outset. With no rival likely to seriously dispute early leadership, the pace will be honest but not pressured, creating a strung-out pattern that tends to suit horses travelling comfortably in behind rather than those coming from very far back. The sheer volume of hold-up horses in this field — including Run For The Border, Ladies Well, Island McCoo, Jouster, Gaoithe Glory, and Charlie's Gift — means the rear of the field will be congested, and true closers will face a traffic problem in the straight. The prominent-to-midfield profile is the sweet spot here: horses able to track Dunany Point without expending early energy, then mount a sustained challenge from two out, are best placed to exploit the single-pace gallop. The field holds significantly more hold-up horses than the track map can accommodate at the rear; Another Challenge, Not So Serious, and Doyen Wolf are genuine hold-up types pushed into midfield slots they will struggle to convert into their natural racing position, diluting the closer threat further. This race shape most clearly favours the prominent racer or efficient traveller in the first half of the field who can pick off a tiring Dunany Point from the second-last fence.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dunany Point Leads, Prominent Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Dunany Point sets a controlled, single-pace gallop and a prominent-tracking rival delivers a clean challenge from two out.
scenarios.body: Dunany Point dictates an uncontested rhythm that lulls the field before the staying test bites in the final half-mile; the winner will be a horse that has tracked in the first four, jumped fluently, and had cover without over-racing. Full Noise, Run For The Border and Ladies Well all profile as horses capable of producing a sustained finishing effort from this position rather than a sharp kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Dunany Point Gallops Rivals Flat
scenarios.trigger: If Dunany Point quickens the tempo mid-race and the hold-up horses find themselves with too much ground to make up on the run-in.
scenarios.body: A stronger early-to-mid gallop from Dunany Point stretches the field and leaves late-closers stranded, rewarding the horse that was close enough throughout to match his stride for stride from three out. Prominent types who jump cleanly and don't burn fuel early — particularly Full Noise and Ballyredinkingston — would inherit an advantage as the hold-up horses find the Roscommon run-in too short for a meaningful challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely moderate and the field bunches, creating enough time for a hold-up horse to weave into contention before the last.
scenarios.body: A muddling gallop compresses the field and gives a horse settled well off the pace the opportunity to find a run down the straight without needing to make up excessive ground; this is the scenario most dependent on traffic breaking right. Run For The Border and Island McCoo are the hold-up types with the best recent good-ground form to capitalise if daylight appears at the right moment.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Dunany Point's lead implodes from three out and the entire field is checked or baulked, creating a scramble.
scenarios.body: A ragged conclusion to the race where jumping errors or fallers disrupt the settled order could hand an advantage to a horse that has been cruising in midfield with something in reserve; Backinabit and Doyen Wolf, though racing out of their natural hold-up role, would have stamina to see out a messy finish. This is the least likely shape but a 19-runner handicap chase on a right-handed track always carries meaningful incident risk.

watchPoints.text: Dunany Point controls everything — if he is allowed a soft lead and jumps cleanly, prominent horses tracking him inside the first five are immediately advantaged; watch for any runner that pressures him early, as that could dramatically alter the pace shape and open the door for hold-up horses.
Run For The Border has no jockey declared — confirm the booking before the off, as a last-minute inexperienced replacement on the top-rated horse would significantly lower his chance of navigating

races.name: Campbell's Bar Ballinlough Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Midnight Moonshine
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who needs things to fall right from the rear; 13d since last run is fine, Good ground suits (13/15 sim-going), but from OR 98 in a 19-runner field the traffic risk is real and finishing position of 5th in last run at 24f Good gives limited encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Midnight Moonshine nonetheless catches the eye as the second-ranked runner in a field of 19, and his experience over today's trip and going is a genuine asset under 168 lb; the concern is that recent form has been patchy at best.

runners_data.name: Decimation
runners_data.note: Aged 11 and 145 days off the track is a significant concern; placemark of 2nd at Heaton Park over 22f is his best recent effort but Heavy/Hurdle ground dominated that form, and only 7/15 sim-going hits suggest Good is not his best surface.
runners_data.comment: Decimation has placed second and third in recent starts, showing he clearly belongs at this level, and having run over today's trip and going he arrives with relevant experience — our rating of 101 puts him right in contention. The concern is 145 days off the track; he'll need to strip fit.

runners_data.name: Kilkee Bay
runners_data.note: Won last time at 22f on Soft and placed at 23f on Good; wears blinkers, 18d since last run is ideal, and a 7-year-old with improving profile — the step up to 3m1f on Good is the one query but style suggests he'll settle and travel.
runners_data.comment: Kilkee Bay arrives on the back of a win two starts ago and a close second last time out, bringing strong recent momentum to this assignment; he has experience of today's trip and going, and at 166 lb the weight is the one factor to negotiate.

runners_data.name: One Way Traffic
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a placed effort at 20f on Good last time; 75d since last run is the only flag, and OR 95 means he carries enough weight to matter — his Soft form is stronger than Good (6/14 sim-going) so conditions are not ideal.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent 75 days, One Way Traffic does at least have going experience to call on, but a fall in recent outings and too many mid-field finishes give pause — the second last time out is the sole bright spot in a patchy recent profile.

runners_data.name: Il Silenzio
runners_data.note: Won at 25f on Good and has three placed efforts at 25f Good in recent hist; wears tongue-tie and pad, 59d since last run is fine, and a 7a amateur rider is notable but the horse's pattern of running on strongly from the rear suits this shape.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back but pulled up three starts back, and that inconsistency is the concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and returns after 59 days off carrying 163 lb, leaving fitness another question mark.

runners_data.name: Sampoet
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will dispute the lead with Kilashee; Good ground specialist (13/14 sim-going) but recent form string of U7485 is concerning for a horse at OR 93 — sets the pace but his winning days appear some time ago.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Sampoet nonetheless rates the one to beat on our figures — ranked top of 19 — and he has experience over today's trip and going. Carrying 163 lb, a clear run after unseating two starts back is the key hope.

runners_data.name: Difficult Decision
runners_data.note: Prominent racer, aged 13, consistent at staying trips but OR 92 and 59d since last run; wears tongue-tie and bar, placed form at 24-25f Good is solid but the age factor and a 7lb claimer make this a tricky winning proposition.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and 59 days off the track are the concerns, but Difficult Decision has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 95 gives him a shout from mid-division despite carrying 162 lb.

runners_data.name: John Storey
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a bleak recent form string of 6PPP; wears tongue-tie and pad, 114d since last run is a concern, and 0 wins and 0 places from 15 similar-going runs makes this a profile to swerve in a competitive field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up three times in that sequence, John Storey arrives 114 days off the track carrying a hefty 162 lb; he has run over today's trip and going before, but his recent record gives more cause for concern than confidence.

runners_data.name: Ballagh Star
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins at 26f on Good; 23d since last run is acceptable, wears tongue-tie and pad, but last run 9th of many at 26f Good and a record of non-completions (two Ps) reduces confidence even if the trip suits.
runners_data.comment: Ninth latest, pulled up twice and unplaced once since winning five starts back, Ballagh Star's recent form makes him very hard to recommend; he has experience of today's distance and going, but ranked 13th of 19 on our figures, he faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Stormy Master
runners_data.note: Won at 26f Good last time out and has three wins from 15 similar-going runs; wears blinkers and his true style is hold-up — 57d since last run is fine, but in this crowded field he is likely to be racing further off the pace than ideal, tempering his winning chance.
runners_data.comment: Stormy Master showed a third two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour, but his ninth last time out and 57-day absence give cause for pause — the 158 lb burden won't help his chance of recapturing that form.

runners_data.name: Made U Look
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse placed at 25f Heavy and with reasonable Good form (3/7 sim-going); 18d since last run, wears a hood — in this field he will struggle to get any closer than midfield, and limited similar-going wins make his chance modest.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win three starts back and retains potential as a lightly raced gelding still open to improvement; 18 days between runs leaves him fresh, and carrying 154 lb is the chief query at this stage.

runners_data.name: Oogum Boogum

runners_data.comment: Oogum Boogum arrives on a quick 13-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going in his favour, and his placed efforts — third two starts back and second three starts back — show ability, but that eighth last time out is a concern under 153 lb.

runners_data.name: Kilashee
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will contest the lead with Sampoet; aged 11 with a recent form string of PP067, wearing no headgear, and 18d since last run — the early energy expenditure in a 19-runner chase at this trip looks likely to find him out in the closing stages.

runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and pulled up on two of her three most recent outings, Captain Kate has serious questions to answer here; ranked 17 of 19 on our figures, only experience over today's trip and going offers any crumb of comfort.

runners_data.note: 637 days absent is a red flag that overrides most other analysis; OR 72, form string of 000RP at 12 years old, tagged as fading in finish — the layoff alone makes this an extremely risky proposition before the stamina question at 3m1f is even considered.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in recent starts and absent for 637 days, Deal Again arrives here with question marks after pulling up last time and refusing the start before that — he's deeply unexposed and open to improvement, but connections have plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Love Like This

runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 19 on our figures, Love Like This faces a stiff ask, arriving off an unplaced effort 11 days ago and winless in her last five starts; that sole win four starts back offers slim hope, though she has distance and going experience and returns quickly fit.

runners_data.name: True Harmony
runners_data.note: A 6-year-old hold-up type flagged for fading in the finish; 12d since last run, best effort a 2nd at 24f Good, but finishing 6th in two recent Good-ground runs — the fade flag in a 3m1f chase with a strong pace is a significant negative.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with two sixths in recent outings and a weight of 152 lb to shoulder, True Harmony faces a stiff task here — ranked 16 of 19 on our figures. He has run over today's trip and going, which offers some grounding, but it is hard to make a case for him.

runners_data.name: Thewaybackhome
runners_data.note: Prominent racer, 5-year-old stepping up to 3m1f having placed at 25f and 22f Good; 25d since last run, wears a hood, trainer 0/4 in 14 days — the youth and progressive form profile (70-342) is appealing if the trip doesn't stretch him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Thewaybackhome at least shows consistency through a run of placings, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; carrying 159 lb and ranked 12th of 19 on our rating, he faces a stiff ask against stronger rivals here.

races.paceDynamic: Sampoet and Kilashee are confirmed front-runners in a 19-runner handicap chase over 3m1f on Good ground at Roscommon, and with both likely to push for the lead from the outset, an honest, pressured gallop is the most probable outcome — neither is a true solo pacesetter, so contested fractions from fence one are expected. The field is unusually hold-up heavy, with Stormy Master, Made U Look, True Harmony, Written In My Soul, Captain Kate, Deal Again and Love Like This all genuine hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map because they cannot all secure their natural rear position in this shape; of these, Stormy Master and Made U Look are most likely to actually settle in midfield with cover, while the others will be shuffled back into the pack. A strongly-run race over an extended trip on Good ground with two contested pacemakers is a classic setup that will expose those who have made their effort too early and reward horses who travel economically in the slipstream before producing a sustained gallop from the third-last. The profile that benefits most clearly is the prominent-to-midfield horse who settles just off the pace without fighting for position and has the class and stamina to grind from the home turn — Oogum Boogum, Thewaybackhome and Il Silenzio fit that frame best.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sampoet and Kilashee set a genuine pace and the field strings out, rewarding those who travel prominently without burning energy early.
scenarios.body: Oogum Boogum and Thewaybackhome are ideally placed to sit just behind the pace, avoid the scrimmage, and produce a sustained finish from the third-last; both have the stamina profile and recent form over this trip on Good ground to grind out a result when rivals are tiring.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace is fierce enough to gut the prominent horses, allowing a true closer to pick up the pieces from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Il Silenzio has a genuine win at 25f on Good and settles well off the pace; One Way Traffic has placed form at this trip on Good and would benefit if the race truly falls apart at the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of Sampoet or Kilashee breaks clear early and the other cries enough, leaving a solo lead at a sustainable gallop that proves unexpectedly good ground for the pace-setter.
scenarios.body: Sampoet has strong Good-ground form (13/14 sim-going runs) and has placed three times in this style; a solo lead at an honest but controlled tempo over 3m1f on Good suits a horse who races prominently and stays every yard.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Attrition Race
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes early traffic trouble, fallers or interference disrupt the pack, and the race becomes a stamina slog won by whoever avoids chaos.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners over fences, Kilkee Bay's recent win form and Difficult Decision's consistent placed record at staying trips give them the durability to grind through a messy, attrition-based finish if the main contenders meet trouble.

watchPoints.text: Sampoet and Kilashee will fight for the early lead in a 19-runner field — watch for a fast, attritional gallop from the first fence that could gut both pace-setters and punish anything that follows them too closely.

With 19 runners over fences at Roscommon, early jumping incidents are probable — Kilashee's recent non-completion record (two Ps in last five) makes him a specific fallers/unseater risk at an early fence that could cause interference.

Deal Again returns from 637 days off the track; at OR 72 and aged 12, a runner this far absent in a competitive 19-runner chase is a dangerous loose-horse risk if he blows up early — watch his jumping in the first mile.

Oogum Boogum has a 7-place count from 15 similar-going runs and sits at OR 83 with a light weight of 153lbs — if the pace genuinely heats up and he travels smoothly in third or fourth, he becomes a serious factor from the third-last.

Trainer John Patrick Ryan has two runners (Kilashee, Love Like This) with a 1/19 strike rate in 14 days — worth monitoring if one of them shows unexpected market support, as yard form appears limited in the current period.
